text: Shannon estimated English at about one bit per character, against log2(26) = 4.7 for uniform letters. What accounts for the gap?
choices: The alphabet is effectively smaller, since some letters almost never occur.
Context: knowing the preceding letters removes most of the uncertainty, which is conditional entropy.
Letter frequencies alone, since e is far more common than z.
The estimate counts only content words, ignoring function words and spaces.
explanation: The progression is 4.7 ignoring frequency, 4.1 with letter frequencies, 3.5 with pairs, and about 1 with real context — H(X|Y) <= H(X), and knowing more never hurts. It also explains why you can read text with the vowels removed, why autocomplete works, and why a language model can predict the next word: prediction and compression are the same problem.
